answer.text: Erodes long option positions over time

explanation.text: The Logic: Theta measures the loss in option value per unit of time, holding other factors constant. Because option premium contains a time-value component that approaches zero at expiry, long option positions are eroded by time decay; option writers (sellers) collect the corresponding decay. The Trap: Theta does not help long option holders — it works against them. It is neither zero nor independent of time; in fact, theta tends to accelerate as expiry nears, especially for at-the-money options. Note: The Portfolio Managers (NISM-Series-XXI-B) workbook discusses option premium, intrinsic value and time value but does not explicitly define theta or state that time decay erodes long option positions. The framing above reflects general industry/regulatory knowledge of option Greeks.
